description: The Wood Dragon in Chinese astrology: personality, Wood element traits, 1964 and 2024 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Wood Dragon is the Dragon born in a Wood year, one of five versions of the fifth animal. It combines the Dragon's vitality with Wood's qualities. Wood Dragon years between 1924 and 2044 are 1964 and 2024. The Dragon's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Wood Dragon personality
paragraphs: A Wood Dragon puts generous, expansive energy into a sign already known for vitality and ambition. The Dragon's fixed element is Earth, and Wood controls Earth, so the stem is said to stir and cultivate the Dragon's grounded core, keeping it from becoming too set in its ways. Wood Dragons are commonly described as creative, curious and inventive, with big ideas and the confidence to pursue them. Compared with other Dragons they are often thought more cooperative and open to advice, though still bold. This mix of drive and imagination can make them pioneering. The pull between Earth's wish for solid ground and Wood's restless growth may also make them impatient with anything that limits their plans.

Wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak. Classical descriptions link it with kindness, idealism and a talent for cooperation: Wood people are often pictured as the ones who start community projects, mentor younger colleagues and believe that most situations can improve with patience and goodwill. The element also carries a strong sense of fairness and a dislike of waste. Its shadow side, according to most readings, is overextension. Like a plant reaching in every direction, a Wood-year person may take on too much, trust too readily or struggle to say no when a cause seems worthwhile.

sections.heading: Wood Dragon at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, the Wood element is usually linked with planning, teaching and collaborative building. Wood-year people are often described as good at seeing how a team could grow and at nurturing the people inside it, which suits roles in education, design, community work, healthcare and any field with a long horizon. They tend to prefer cooperation over rivalry. The traditional warning is about scope: a Wood stem can start more ventures than it can finish, so firm priorities and honest deadlines usually serve it well.

The Wood Dragon thinks in decades and enjoys rallying others behind a long undertaking. It is commonly linked with urban planning, school leadership, publishing, social enterprise and architecture, fields where a vision has to be shared before it can be built. Genuine latitude and colleagues who can translate big sketches into budgets suit it well. Unlike some Dragons, it usually credits the team generously when things go right. In relationships, the Wood Dragon is magnanimous and inspiring, cheering a partner's ambitions as eagerly as its own. It wants admiration and a lively intellectual companion. Tension surfaces when its many schemes crowd the calendar, and a partner begins to feel like one ambitious project among several.

sections.heading: Wood Dragon years and dates
paragraphs: Wood Dragon years in the Lunar New Year table run from February 13, 1964 to February 1, 1965 and from February 10, 2024 to January 28, 2025. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1964 anyone born before Feb 13 is a Water Rabbit, not a Wood Dragon. Sixty years separate each Wood Dragon year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Wood Dragon year is Yang, matching the Dragon's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Jia-Chen: Jia is the yang Wood stem and Chen is the Dragon's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Water Rabbit year (before February 13, 1964) and the Water Rabbit year (before February 10, 2024), and births in the weeks after each Wood Dragon year ends belong to the Wood Snake. The new year itself fell on a Thursday in 1964 and Saturday in 2024.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Wood Dragon
paragraphs: Many readings point Wood Dragons towards finishing as their main area for development. Their imagination generates projects quickly, so a habit of completing one before launching the next keeps credibility high. They tend to admire their own vision, and inviting critique early can save effort later. Wood Dragons also respond well to mentoring roles, which channel their generosity and ideas into other people's growth. Since the combination likes to be admired, seeking quiet satisfaction in well-done work rather than applause is a useful discipline. When it balances scope with patience, a Wood Dragon can build things of lasting worth.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Wood Dragon shares the Dragon's San He trine with the Rat and Monkey (the Water trine), its Liu He bond with the Rooster, and its Liu Chong clash with the Dog. The element adds a second layer: another Wood sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Wood in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Wood Dragon years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1964 (from February 13, 1964) and 2024 (from February 10, 2024). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Wood Dragon's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Wood and the Dragon's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles wood controls Earth. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Wood Dragon?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rat and Monkey (San He) and the Rooster (Liu He). The Dog is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Wood Dragon called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Jia-Chen. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Wood stem Jia, followed by its earthly branch, here Chen for the Dragon, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Wood Dragon different from other Dragons?
faq.answer: All Dragons share vitality, ambition and confidence. The Wood year element changes the tone: wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak.
